The test image shows a severely diseased tomato leaf with large, irregular dark brown/black necrotic lesions covering most of the leaf surface, with some remaining green and yellow-green tissue. The necrosis appears to have a somewhat water-soaked, greasy appearance. This pattern is consistent with Late Blight.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

**Analysis:**

**Test image features:**
- Tomato leaf with massive, irregular dark brown/black necrotic lesions covering ~80% of the leaf
- Some remaining green and yellowish tissue
- Lesions appear somewhat water-soaked/greasy at margins
- Leaf is curling, very severe damage
- No concentric ring/target pattern (rules out Early Blight)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- No small dark specks with yellow halos (rules out Bacterial Speck)

**Reference image comparison (Late Blight):**
- The reference shows a similar large, irregular dark brown necrotic area spreading across the leaf with healthy green tissue remaining
- Same general background (gray surface), same style of necrosis spreading
- Test image is more advanced/severe but matches the same progression pattern of large irregular brown-black lesions

The large irregular coalescing dark lesions without concentric rings, combined with the water-soaked appearance and severe tissue destruction, strongly matches Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans).
